descriptionChirho: Clothing or apparel as a collective term for garments worn; used in the NT for the general concept of what one wears, including in contexts of wealth and adornment (Luke 7:25 'splendid clothing', Luke 9:29 garments becoming dazzling white at the Transfiguration). Multilingual evidence treats both clusters as the same concept: Spanish 'vestimenta/vestido/ropa', Hindi 'vastra/poshak', Arabic 'malabisa/libasiyan/rida'iya', Korean 'uibok/ot', Swahili 'mavazi/vazi'. The dative/nominative/genitive forms (N-DMS, N-NMS, N-GMS) and accusative form (N-AMS) are grammatical case variation of one unified sense.
